correctness.rationale: For positive x,y, gcd=1 and x odd convert the divisibilities to xy|(x²+2y²+1). The quotient k≥3. The 2-adic valuation of x²+1 separates odd y (k≡4 mod8) from y≡2 mod4 (odd k). Integral positive Vieta conjugations in the odd chamber strictly descend according to sign of x²−2y², terminating uniquely at (1,1) and k=4. Completing squares gives u²−2y²=−1 and x=2y±u. The even chamber is exactly s²−(k²−8)t²=−1, y=2t and x=kt±s, with all parity and positivity converses checked; k=3 yields only (3,2), solvable odd k≥5 infinite by units. For primes p≡7 mod8, the two roots k²≡8 mod p are impossible because −1 is nonsquare. CRT over p≤√log X, the product bound and the Mertens progression estimate yield ≪X/√loglogX. Independently counted 15 pairs in 1≤x,y≤350 and parameters {3,4,5,7,9,11}; this is corroboration, not the infinite proof.
